cases.sql: SET TimeZone='UTC';SET IntervalStyle='postgres'
CREATE TABLE calendar_values (id integer PRIMARY KEY, base timestamptz, span interval)
CREATE VIEW calendar_view AS SELECT timestamptz '2024-03-09 17:00:00+00' + interval '1 day' AS v
CREATE TABLE calendar_defaults (v timestamptz DEFAULT (timestamptz '2024-03-09 17:00:00+00' + interval '1 day'))
CREATE FUNCTION calendar_ny(v timestamptz, i interval) RETURNS timestamptz LANGUAGE SQL SET TimeZone='America/New_York' AS 'SELECT v+i'
PREPARE calendar_prepared(timestamptz,interval) AS SELECT (timestamptz '2024-03-09 17:00:00+00' + interval '1 day') AT TIME ZONE 'UTC' AS constant, ($1 + $2) AT TIME ZONE 'UTC' AS runtime
CREATE TABLE calendar_generated_bad (v timestamptz, shifted timestamptz GENERATED ALWAYS AS (v+interval '1 day') STORED)
CREATE TABLE calendar_generated_good (v timestamp, shifted timestamp GENERATED ALWAYS AS (v+interval '1 day') STORED)
INSERT INTO calendar_generated_good(v) VALUES ('2024-03-09 12:00:00')
CREATE TABLE calendar_frames (id integer PRIMARY KEY, v timestamptz)
SET TimeZone='UTC'
SELECT id,(base+span) AT TIME ZONE 'UTC' AS added,(base-span) AT TIME ZONE 'UTC' AS subtracted,(span+base) AT TIME ZONE 'UTC' AS reversed FROM calendar_values ORDER BY id
SELECT v AT TIME ZONE 'UTC' FROM calendar_view
EXECUTE calendar_prepared('2024-03-09 17:00:00+00','1 day')
INSERT INTO calendar_defaults DEFAULT VALUES RETURNING v AT TIME ZONE 'UTC'
SELECT id,calendar_ny(base,span) AT TIME ZONE 'UTC',current_setting('TimeZone') FROM calendar_values ORDER BY id
SELECT * FROM calendar_generated_good

SELECT id,count(*) OVER (ORDER BY v ASC RANGE BETWEEN interval '1 day' PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS calendar,count(*) OVER (ORDER BY v ASC RANGE BETWEEN interval '24 hours' PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS elapsed,count(*) OVER (ORDER BY v ASC RANGE BETWEEN CURRENT ROW AND interval '1 day' FOLLOWING) AS following FROM calendar_frames ORDER BY id
